Redis, Beyond Caching
Four production patterns: caching, rate limiting, distributed locks and event broadcasting

Why they all work: Redis runs every command, and every Lua script, on one thread. Each one is atomic.
USE CASE 1 · CACHING
Cache-aside, with a stampede lock
npm run demo:cache
WHEN TO USE
  • Read-heavy data that can be seconds stale
  • Product pages, profiles, config, prices
  • The database is the slow, costly part
HOW REDIS SUPPORTS IT
  • Miss: load from DB, HSET + EXPIRE
  • On write: DEL the key, don't update it
  • Lua SET NX PX lock: one request reloads
  • TTL jitter + an eviction policy when full
CODE · TypeScript · ioredis
const hit = await redis.hgetall(key); if (Object.keys(hit).length) return hit; // ~0.5 ms const token = randomUUID(); const won = await redis.eval(ACQUIRE, 1, // SET NX PX   `lock:${key}`, token, 2000); if (!won) return waitForCache(key); // poll, no DB hit try {   const row = await db.products.find(id); // ~300 ms   await redis.multi().hset(key, row)     .expire(key, 300 + jitter(30)).exec();   return row; } finally {   await redis.eval(RELEASE, 1, `lock:${key}`, token); }
Source: redis.io/docs/latest/develop/use-cases/cache-aside/nodejs
USE CASE 1 · CACHING · THE HARD PART
"There are only two hard things in Computer Science: cache invalidation and naming things."
Phil Karlton
A cached key leaves in one of three ways. Then the next read misses and cache-aside refills it.
1 · YOU DELETE IT
The data changed
DEL key
On every write to the database. Nothing stale is served.
2 · IT EXPIRES
Time is up
EXPIRE key 300
How long can this be stale? That decides the TTL.
3 · REDIS EVICTS IT
Memory is full
maxmemory-policy
Redis picks a key to drop. Which one? Next slide.
USE CASE 1 · CACHING · WHEN MEMORY IS FULL
How Redis picks a key to evict
USE CASE 1 · CACHING · EVICTION POLICY
Choosing the right policy: three questions
1
Can this data be rebuilt from the source of truth?
No → noeviction
queues, streams, sessions; alert on memory
Yes → keep going
it is a cache
2
Do cache keys and durable keys share one instance?
Yes → volatile-lfu
TTL on cache keys only; better: split instances
No → allkeys-*
every key is fair game
3
What does the traffic look like?
allkeys-lfu
stable hot set, batch scans
allkeys-lru
recency matters: feeds
allkeys-random
no pattern
CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lfu · then watch INFO stats: keyspace_hits, keyspace_misses, evicted_keys
USE CASE 1 · CACHING · REAL LIFE
Flash sale: memory is full. What goes?
One Redis for an online shop. The sale starts, product pages flood the cache, memory runs out.
product:*
Cached product pages
TTL 5 min
Nothing. It reloads from the database.
SAFE TO EVICT
session:*
Logged-in users
No TTL
The user is logged out.
MUST NOT BE EVICTED
cart:*
Shopping carts
No TTL
The cart is empty and the sale is lost.
MUST NOT BE EVICTED
The real question is not LRU or LFU. It is: can Redis tell cache from state?
LIVE DEMO · FLASH SALE
Same sale, three policies
npm run demo:flashsale
allkeys-lru
Carts and sessions are the oldest keys, so they go first. Only ~80 of 300 carts survive.
"My cart is empty!"
noeviction
Nothing is deleted. Once memory is full, every write fails: new orders get OOM errors.
"Checkout is broken!"
volatile-lru + TTL on cache keys
Only product pages are evicted. All 300 carts and sessions survive.
Nobody notices
Rule: Redis can only protect what it can tell apart. Put TTLs on cache keys, or give cache and state separate instances.
USE CASE 2 · RATE LIMITING
Throttle and block abusive IPs
npm run demo:ratelimit
WHEN TO USE
  • Quotas per IP, user or API key
  • Login brute force, scrapers, costly APIs
  • Shared across every app instance, sub-ms
HOW REDIS SUPPORTS IT
  • INCR + PEXPIRE in one atomic Lua call
  • Sorted-set sliding window for precision
  • block:<ip> EX 60 for repeat offenders
  • One thread: no lost counts under load
CODE · TypeScript · ioredis
-- FIXED: KEYS[1] = rl:<ip>:<window>, ARGV[1] = ms local n = redis.call('INCR', KEYS[1]) if n == 1 then   redis.call('PEXPIRE', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]) end return n // middleware, on every request if (await redis.exists(`block:${ip}`)) return deny(403); const n = await redis.eval(FIXED, 1, key, 10_000); if (n > LIMIT * 2)   await redis.set(`block:${ip}`, "1", "EX", 60); if (n > LIMIT) return deny(429, retryAfter); next();
Source: redis.io/docs/latest/develop/use-cases/rate-limiter
USE CASE 3 · DISTRIBUTED LOCKING
One writer at a time
npm run demo:lock
WHEN TO USE
  • Payments + inventory: charge, then reserve
  • Run a cron or token refresh exactly once
  • Flash sales: many buyers, few items
HOW REDIS SUPPORTS IT
  • SET key token NX PX ttl, one command
  • Release: Lua compare-and-delete on token
  • TTL > worst case; fence writes via INCR
  • Just a counter? Lua check-and-DECR, no lock
CODE · TypeScript · ioredis
const token = randomUUID(); const ok = await redis.set("lock:sku:ps5", token,   "PX", 2000, "NX"); // "OK" or null if (!ok) return retryWithJitter(); try {   await chargeCardAndReserveStock(order); } finally {   await redis.eval(RELEASE, 1, "lock:sku:ps5", token); } -- RELEASE: only delete the lock if it is still ours if redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) == ARGV[1] then   return redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1]) end return 0
Source: redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/patterns/distributed-locks
USE CASE 4 · BROADCASTING EVENTS
Live fan-out vs. must-deliver
npm run demo:broadcast
WHEN TO USE
  • Pub/Sub: presence, typing, live dashboards
  • Streams: notifications, chat history
  • Many nodes need the same event at once
HOW REDIS SUPPORTS IT
  • PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE; SPUBLISH in a cluster
  • XREAD from last seen ID after reconnect
  • Consumer groups split work; MAXLEN caps it
CODE · TypeScript · ioredis
// Pub/Sub: live only, offline clients miss it await sub.subscribe("chat:room:42"); sub.on("message", (_ch, msg) => ws.send(msg)); await redis.publish("chat:room:42", text);   // Stream: history + catch-up on reconnect await redis.xadd("chat:42:log", "MAXLEN", "~", 10_000,   "*", "user", userId, "text", text); const missed = await redis.xread("COUNT", 100,   "STREAMS", "chat:42:log", lastSeenId);
Source: redis.io/docs/latest/develop/use-cases/streaming · redis.io/docs/latest/develop/use-cases/pub-sub
USE CASE 4 · PICK YOUR TRANSPORT
Redis vs Kafka vs SQS
Option
Best for
Pros
Cons
Redis Pub/Sub
Presence, typing, live dashboards, cache invalidation
Sub-ms fan-out, nothing to set up, pattern subscriptions
No persistence or ack: offline means missed
Redis Streams
Notifications, chat history, job queues, hours to days of events
Consumer groups, ack + reclaim, replay, on the Redis you already run
Bounded by RAM; one stream lives on one shard
Apache Kafka
Event backbone, analytics pipelines, weeks of retention
Disk-backed, partitioned, very high throughput, replay by offset
Brokers, partitions and rebalancing to operate
Amazon SQS
Decoupled jobs on AWS, serverless workers
Fully managed, auto-scales, DLQs, retention up to 14 days
No replay; fan-out needs SNS; FIFO 300 msg/s default
Rule of thumb: already running Redis and retention is hours to days? Start with Streams. Need weeks of history or a company-wide event bus? Kafka. Want zero ops on AWS? SQS.
Sources: redis.io use-cases/streaming · aws.amazon.com/sqs/faqs · Kafka default retention log.retention.hours = 168
USE CASE 4 · STREAMS + CONSUMER GROUPS
A consumer group, step by step
LIVE DEMO · CONSUMER GROUPS · FOUR TERMINALS
Kill a consumer, lose nothing
T1 · live XINFO view
npm run demo:streams:monitor
T2 · healthy consumer
… consumer -- --name alice
T3 · will crash after 5 messages
… consumer -- --name bob --die-after 5
T4 · orders, every 25th is poison
npm run demo:streams:producer -- --rate 3
1
alice and bob split the orders: each message goes to exactly one of them.
2
bob crashes. The monitor shows his pending count stuck and idle time climbing.
3
demo:streams:reclaim -- --watch recovers bob's work and dead-letters the poison.
4
--name report --group analytics --from 0 replays all history in a new group.
FOUR TAKEAWAYS
1. Cache-aside: DEL on write, jitter TTLs, lock the reload of hot keys.
2. Rate limits: INCR + PEXPIRE in one Lua script; block repeat offenders.
3. Locks: SET NX PX with a token, release by token, fence the write.
4. Pub/Sub for live, Streams when nobody may miss it, Kafka for weeks.
